checks: Parallel threshold adjustment reduces any containing halfspace to a through-mark halfspace. Reflection preserves the measure, and any closed halfspace containing the midpoint of the reflected pair contains at least one of its endpoints. Therefore restricting to height 1/2 preserves the maximum.

All nonzero continuous normals reduce by reflection and positive scaling to x−1/2≥u(z−1). The four trace masses sum to a+b/2+(b−a)q(u)+a q(2u) using nonatomic symmetric tails. Since b≥a, this is at least a+b/2, with equality for u>1/2.

The pure-base orientations at z=1 include the entire boundary fiber and have masses a+b and a+2b. The opposite middle base is obtained by base reflection. The extreme caps retain only half an outer fiber of mass a, so those sites cannot raise the maximum.

overlap.comparison: The identical expression b/2+a occurs for four ordinary-volume fibers A,B,B,D with equal outer volumes and outer bodies contained in centrally symmetric B. Arbitrary common nonatomic conditional laws and independent external weights cannot be instantiated as those uniform-volume traces, and the new conclusion applies directly to later nonuniform midpoint laws.
The rank-one symmetric-fiber theorem gives a lower bound for ordinary volume and allows general supports, without the exact four-fiber formula or the present class of probability kernels.
